title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the summary diagram (133) from the previous page. That diagram involves the 'loop-equation' group scheme M_{ρ,σ} over Z and its index-2 subgroup M°_{ρ,σ}.

Setting and notation:
- ρ is the order-3/6 elliptic datum. T_ρ is the norm-type torus attached to Z[ρ], with T_ρ(Z) = μ_6 ≅ Z/6.
- σ is the order-4 datum. T_σ is the torus attached to Z[i], with T_σ(Z) = μ_4 ≅ Z/4. N'_σ is a normaliser-type extension of T_σ.
- G is a GL_2-type group with SG and PG; R_{ρ,σ} is ≅ S'T_ρ × SN'_σ × G_m.

The previous page established the following.
- The centraliser scheme Cent(M°) equals R° ≅ ST_ρ × ST_σ × G_m (dimension 3).
- Cent(M) ≅ S'T_ρ × μ_2 × G_m (dimension 2).
- The horizontal arrows of (133) are quotients by μ_2×μ_2 and by μ_2 respectively.

This page says that diagram (133) is valid over any base. In the 'absolute modular case' (base Z), taking integral points gives homomorphisms along the two horizontal arrows, between the finite groups (134):
- Cent(M°_{ρ,σ})(Z) ≅ Z/6 × Z/4 × {±1}, of order 48.
- Cent(M_{ρ,σ})(Z) ≅ Z/6 × {±1} × {±1}, of order 24.
Grothendieck notes that these groups have subgroups of index 2.

He then recalls the elementary abelian subgroup Σ = {±1}^3 of Cent(M_{ρ,σ})(Z), of order 8. It consists of the ±1 inside μ_6 together with the two sign factors, and it has index 3. Σ plays a special role arithmetically because there is a canonical homomorphism (136), boxed: M_{0,3}^~ → M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ.

My reading of (136): it is the arithmetic/Galois-theoretic object attached to M_{0,3}, plausibly the profinite (Galois–Teichmüller-type) group acting on the profinite completion of the modular group. That group maps to the Ẑ-points of the loop-equation group scheme, but only up to sign ambiguities. Those ambiguities come from choices of lifts, i.e. square roots and orientation choices, and they are measured exactly by Σ.

The purpose is to bookkeep the finite centralisers, so that the arithmetic action is well defined modulo a canonical finite group. The next page then begins section 7°, a recapitulative list of the homomorphisms involving M_{ρ,σ}.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The orders are consistent: |Cent(M)(Z)| = 24 and |Σ| = 8, so the index 3 is correct.
The phrase 'qui ont des sous-groupes d'indice 2' is vague. Presumably it refers to the images, or to the intersections with M°, under the horizontal maps; the exact statement is not spelled out.
The precise meaning of M_{0,3}^~ and of the 'canonical homomorphism' (136) is not justified on this page.

ideas.what: Computation of integral points of the centraliser group schemes of M_{ρ,σ} and M°_{ρ,σ} over Z, as products of μ_6, μ_4 and ±1
ideas.modern_name: Integral points of tori and finite group schemes attached to Z[ρ], Z[i] (units/roots of unity of CM orders)

ideas.what: Canonical homomorphism from the arithmetic group attached to M_{0,3} into Ẑ-points of the loop-equation group scheme, modulo the sign group Σ = {±1}^3
ideas.modern_name: Galois/Grothendieck–Teichmüller action on the profinite modular group, encoded via an algebraic group scheme over Z; sign ambiguities of GT-parameters
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT, 1990), Ihara, Schneps, Lochak–Schneps for related GT/SL2 actions
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme sketches Galois action on the Teichmüller tower; this specific map does not appear there to my knowledge

missed.claim: The arithmetic action attached to M_{0,3} is landed in the Ẑ-points of an algebraic group scheme M_{ρ,σ} over Z, built from the CM tori of Z[ρ] and Z[i]. It is well defined modulo an explicit finite sign group Σ that lies in the centraliser. This is a group-scheme packaging of the 'loop equations' that I do not recognise in the GT literature, which works with profinite groups directly.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give an algebraic-group model for the GT/Galois action on the profinite modular group, with a canonical normalisation of sign ambiguities. However, the construction depends on earlier pages not visible here.

deep.surprise_reason: Most of the page is routine bookkeeping of finite integral points. Only the boxed map (136) hints at a nonstandard arithmetic packaging, and it is merely stated, with no derivation.
transcription_corrections: The groups in (134) are 'Cent' (centraliser, underlined), not 'Aut': Cent(M_{ρ,σ̊})(Z) and Cent(M_{ρ,σ})(Z).
'contenu dans Cent(M_{ρ,σ})(Z) (d'ailleurs d'indice 3)' — the transcription 'pas[?]' is probably a misreading.
'joue un rôle particulier dans l'situation arithmétique' should read 'dans la situation arithmétique'.
